Information since October signals a strong labor market and moderate growth, but with below-target inflation and weakness in business investment and exports. In New Keynesian frameworks (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), inflation is tied to real marginal cost from labor markets; the coexistence of tight employment and sub-2% inflation, alongside low market-based inflation compensation, is consistent with a flat Phillips curve and anchored expectations (Rudebusch and Svensson; Ang and Piazzesi on term-structure signals). Steady policy rates with continued T-bill purchases and repo operations to maintain ample reserves align with modern implementation practice (Goodfriend, 2002) and support smooth policy transmission without necessarily signaling additional easing. While solid job gains point to ongoing expansion via Okun’s law, subdued capex is consistent with credit-market amplification and financing constraints affecting investment (Gertler; references noting investment sensitivity to the financial system). Net tone: mildly positive but cautious.
